reviews.author: muerte black
reviews.text:
Like the person that gave it 1 star, I had a few issues with the people walking through my site when the walkway was just on the other side. Bikes all over the trails where signs had no bikes and had to move out of the way or get ran over.

The worst of all, at least in the south loop was the constant smell of sewer. If I could have afforded to cancel and move I would have, but I was stuck. I can't say for the other loops but will never do the south loop again. Rotten Eggs La Pine.

Oh yeah, almost forgot the jerks that had a trailer and truck too big for their spot and stuck out making it hard to go down the narrow road on a turn to get around them. Even made the poor people next to them have to back in a pull through spot with their large trailer because of the jerks. They were here most of the time with their truck sticking out and the state and park workers did nothing. Have them park in the overflow, move as there were plenty of spots. But no, I don't think I will come here again as I just got another flood of sewer smell. HORRIBLE!!!

reviews.author: Jeff Bhend
reviews.text: This campground is really nice. I would not stay here again until they have phone service and WiFi. Unfortunately in today’s world being able to use your phone has become a priority. People need to be able to do things on their phones these days.

reviews.author: Robert Carlton Miller
reviews.text: This is a Fantastic year-round campground. Great experience, no bothers & Hot Showers! I was camped alongside the river so a few individuals just pop up or come cruising through on bikes but it was No Worries.

reviews.author: Brian Turner
reviews.text: The only complaint we had was the slope of our campsite. We should have done a little more research so that’s on us but overall great experience…campsite 123 btw 😃

reviews.author: Jade Hampton
reviews.text:
I’ll never stay here again. The website doesn’t give the location of your camping spot within the campground and No photo was provided on the site. Had I known the spot was right at the entrance across from the cabins I would have never booked it.

The cabin dwellers kept cutting between mine and another renters camp spot to access the toilets instead of using the designated paths. At one point they walked directly through my spot between my car and the picnic table. This is poor camp etiquette and needs to be posted in the cabins as they did not read the courtesy rules at the entrance. I asked them to stop and they did not. They also wore headlamps and shined them into cars, campers and tents. My God…point your head down if your wearing one of those things!

The electricity didn’t work at my spot either. A previous renter bent the plugs preventing anything from being plugged into it.

I camped in the middle of October during the middle of the week and every spot was booked. The North and Middle campgrounds are shut down to make management easier on staff. So expect crowds and noise.

If you have a camper or trailer to sleep in it’s probably fine, the roads are very narrow. I would avoid tent camping due to the noise.

I left after one night due to lack of sleep from the cabin renters and lack of electricity. What a waste.

reviews.author: Brenda T
reviews.text: Very clean and beautiful park. Have to see the Big Tree, is worth the trip. The river is quite beautiful too, very serene.

reviews.author: DeEtte F
reviews.text: This is my favorite campground in the Oregon state park system! The sites are very spacious with lots of space between them. Lots of pull-through sites that accommodate long RVs. I also love all the hiking and biking trails. Very easy walk to the Deschutes River from the campground.

reviews.author: knnj
reviews.text: This park is incredible clean and very well organized. Highly recommended for camping and recreation.

reviews.author: fireinjunjoe
reviews.text: We stayed for 2 nights in our RV. Spaces are good size and it's a state park so it's well maintained. Paved roads/ pads.Our spot was about 50 yards to the Deschutes River through the trees.

reviews.author: 2rollon
reviews.text:
Friend and I stayed here for 2 nights. Clean bathrooms, nice showered with hot water. Camp host friendly. Clean campground. A lot to see and do in the area. We were gone most of the day exploring and slept well at night.

We went to lava lands, saw the Big Tree and drove to some lakes in the area.

We would stay again.

reviews.author: Shirley G
reviews.text:
Whether you are a single, couple or family this park does not disappoint. The entire park is well managed and I found park hosts to be friendly and helpful.

LaPine State Park-Full service site including onsite sewer was $64 for two nights including the $8 reservation fee. By accident we reserved site #39 that was a previous campground host site. It was large with two fire pits and two tables. Like Tumalo the hiking is superb and some trails are along the river.

There are three campsite loops at LaPine Park. The North loop is the oldest and only 20 amp. Showers are clean but one can see a bit of aging. Our site was in the South loop with 50 amp and I did not have to level. (22’ Outlook Class C no slides) The handicap shower/bath room was amazing. Although not handicapped I used the shower at 6 am. One room with toilet, sink, mirror and large shower area. Great for families with children.

We had campfires all four evenings. There was enough branches and firewood in the area surrounding our campsite that we used for firewood. You are allowed to bring your own firewood as long as it was grown in Oregon.

A huge day use area across the road from the campsites has amazing trails and frisbee golf area.

Hiking trails won't disappoint and you can choose a trail that follows the river. Sites are paved and the South loop sites appeared to be the most level. I would not hesitate being self contained to reserve a tent site if RV sites were full.

Cabins for rent and some have showers!

reviews.author: Aaron N
reviews.text: Had a great time, got in on a Sunday and stayed 3 nights in a row. Campground nearly full, yet not real noisy. Sites well-spaced and privatized. Located in beautiful forest setting, so much to do in such a short distance. Cold stream to swim in, refreshing on an average summer's day there.

reviews.author: camper-884665
reviews.text: This might be my favorite state park campsite yet. Beautiful park, very clean and well-maintained. There is a camp host for each other the three loops. The bathhouse is clean and the showers have hot water. The scenery is gorgeous. There are bike trails and hiking trails throughout the park. The Big Tree is cool. The Deschutes River is lovely. Loved it!

reviews.author: camper-796293
reviews.text: We stayed one night because we are on a road trip and have several locations to see on our journey. We couldn't have been more happy to find this gem on our way to crater Lake. During peak season I'm sure you would not be able to just pull up and pay for the night without reservation. Good clean bathrooms and showers. Full hookups and large paved flat spots in the south loop. Parts of the campground were closed so I couldn't speak to those areas but it was a lovely state park, great price and very cute cabins for rent also. Would definitely stay agin but for longer. 😊

reviews.author: Tom & Shirley
reviews.text: We spent a week and enjoyed biking the trails until the snow came and provided beautiful snow scenes. Quiet setting this time of year. Made the most of our electric hook up for heat as nights were below freezing. Showers have hot water but shower house is not warm so time your shower for the warmer time of the day this time of year. Verizon cell was one bar - only good for phone calls.

reviews.author: DebDan
reviews.text: Stayed 3 nights, no problem with power, super clean CG, Oregon state parks are great. Very nice!

reviews.author: Ashley
reviews.text: The dog park is perfect, and the trails are great. Cougar sighting 5 July, 22; just know how to act in cougar country. There are no trash receptacles in the loops, but there is trash, mixed recycling, and a dump station at the ranger booth. They do offer small cans for pet waste in each loop. The FHU loops have spaces that are closer together than the E/W sites. It's hot in the summer, but there is great fun to be had on the beautiful Deschutes river! Verizon is capable, but slow: 5.64 download, 0.29 upload (no TikTok, even with a booster). Last year we ran into racist graffiti here that was quickly covered by park staff. It's eastern Oregon...

reviews.author: moff
reviews.text: Great place full hook ups and 50amp lots of hiking and biking trails only reason didn't give five stars is trying to work while there really tuff 1 bar while time
